{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeioW0w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIDqHs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 317, "title": "Make Create Subgraph discoverable with multi-select, simple dialog, and editable inferred ports", "body": "## Goal

Make **Create Subgraph** understandable and easy to use without changing what a reusable subgraph means or breaking existing graph connections.

Agreed UX:
1. Select multiple processing nodes directly on the Graph Editor canvas.
2. See the selection clearly and a contextual **Create Subgraph** action when multiple nodes are selected.
3. Open a simple creation dialog showing the selected nodes, enter a name, and create. Inputs/outputs are **automatically inferred**, but an optional **Edit input / output ports** section allows advanced manual edits.
4. The internal node graph and all existing external connections remain functionally equivalent after extraction.

Keep the ability to reuse/edit the created subgraph through Graph Library and Add Node.

## Current implementation

- [`extension/graph-editor.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js): `selectDetails(node, connection, extend)` already supports multi-selection through `multiSelection`, currently mainly **Shift+click / Shift+Enter** on node headings; selected headings receive `selected-node` class. `this.createButton` is currently inside **Graph actions (…)** and enabled for any nonempty selection.
- `createSubgraph()` calls `extractSubgraph(this.draft, this.multiSelection, id, this.definitions)`. It then opens a modal with name and the entire **Exposed ports** editor expanded by default (`renderPortEditor()`), which is difficult to understand.
- [`extension/subgraphs.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/subgraphs.js): `extractSubgraph()` keeps selected internal nodes/internal edges, infers exposed ports from crossing parent edges, creates a Subgraph instance and remaps the parent edges. It requires a connected selection and excludes concrete input and output destinations and nested subgraphs.
- [`docs/extension-graph.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md) documents these behaviors.
- [#299](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/299) is replacing manual Save with autosave/Undo-Redo; coordinate subgraph creation and parent draft persistence with that work.

## Required interaction changes

### 1. Multi-selection, platform conventions and discoverability

- A plain click on a node heading selects that single node; clicking it again or clicking blank canvas/Escape clears selection in accordance with existing expected behavior.
- The following modified clicks **all toggle the clicked node into/out of the multi-selection** (noncontiguous, not range selection):
  - **Windows/Linux:** `Shift+click` **or** `Ctrl+click`.
  - **macOS:** `Shift+click` **or** `Command (Meta)+click`.
- Use a single underlying toggle-selection path regardless of modifier; do not allow modifiers to trigger OS/browser shortcuts, and do not override **Control+click on macOS**, which may act as native secondary/right-click.
- Preserve keyboard selection, including existing **Shift+Enter**. Keep keyboard focus, accessible pressed/selected state and a usable way to unselect; avoid relying on color alone.
- Clearly highlight selected nodes and provide a concise **N nodes selected** indicator.
- When **2 or more nodes** are selected, expose a contextual **Create Subgraph** button prominently near the selection/Inspector (not hidden only in the ellipsis menu). The button should not appear for zero or one selected nodes, and should not obstruct canvas controls. Prefer removing the redundant command from the generic Graph actions menu so there is one obvious entry point.
- If selected nodes are not an eligible connected processing group, explain **why** in concise plain language at the point of creation (or disabled state), not a generic uncaught error. Preserve the underlying graph validation and selection until the user can correct it.
- Preserve existing node drag, keyboard movement, connection/port selection, scrolling/zoom and all single-node inspector settings.

### 2. Simplified Create Subgraph dialog

Default dialog should have:
- Title **Create Subgraph** and one short explanation such as “Combine the selected nodes into a reusable Subgraph.”
- **Subgraph name** field, required, initially sensible/prefilled (existing `Shared processing` is acceptable).
- **Included nodes** compact read-only summary (names/types and/or IDs, e.g. Text Formatter, Text Summary) and count, based on the actual selected nodes.
- **Connections preserved** confirmation and an accurate count of **automatically inferred inputs and outputs** (do not invent a fixed 1-in/1-out assumption; zero or multiple crossing ports are possible).
- An initially **collapsed** `Edit input / output ports` disclosure, not an always-expanded port-ID/endpoint form.
- **Cancel** and **Create Subgraph** actions, with clear validation and error reporting; no unnecessary help prose.

### 3. Advanced exposed ports editing remains available

- Expanding **Edit input / output ports** reveals the existing advanced functionality: rename exposed input/output ports, add/remove exposed ports, and choose a valid internal endpoint where supported. Keep type inference from endpoint and stable port IDs.
- The automatically inferred port mapping should already be valid without editing; opening and closing the advanced section should not mutate it.
- If the user edits an automatically inferred port, **preserve the original crossing-edge semantics**: never silently disconnect, misroute, drop, or change the data type of a parent edge. Either keep its stable exposed-port identity and valid endpoint or clearly reject a change that would break connections. User-added optional exposed ports can remain unconnected in the parent.
- Keep `assertSubgraph`, `assertGraph`, `resolveSubgraphs`, and compatibility/parent-reference safeguards authoritative. Invalid advanced changes must be explained and must not partially commit a broken parent or shared definition.

## Extraction behavior / persistence

- Preserve selected node IDs, settings, positions (as appropriate), **all internal edges**, and the original connectivity across the extraction boundary. The parent graph should contain one new Subgraph instance in place of the selected group, with crossing edges remapped automatically. Fan-out/repeated crossing endpoints must remain correct.
- Only eligible connected processing nodes may be extracted; concrete sources/outputs and nested Subgraphs remain disallowed under the existing one-level design.
- The new shared definition is saved into Graph Library; it appears in the Subgraphs category of Add Node and can be reused in other graphs.
- Preserve the existing semantics of **Edit Subgraph** and the editable exposed interface after creation. Do not require the user to expand advanced settings for a normal creation.
- Creation is a cross-entry operation: do not silently lose the parent edit or create unusable dangling definitions if persistence/revision checks fail. For **#299 Auto Save + Undo/Redo**, ensure the parent replacement is correctly tracked and auto-saved, while Undo of the parent replacement does not delete a shared definition referenced elsewhere. Preserve existing concurrent/stale revision protections and draft recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple selection works with Shift/Ctrl on Windows/Linux and Shift/Command on macOS. Existing Shift+Enter keyboard selection still works; macOS Control+click keeps native behavior.
- [ ] Selected nodes are unmistakable, selection count is visible and contextual Create Subgraph is discoverable with 2+ selected nodes. No redundant unconditional command confusing users in Graph actions.
- [ ] Eligible connected processing selection opens an easy-to-understand dialog showing true included nodes, inferred input/output counts and preservation of connections, without showing advanced port fields by default.
- [ ] Users can optionally expand detailed inputs/outputs and change valid port names/endpoints or add/remove ports; invalid changes are rejected with actionable explanations before storage is modified.
- [ ] Internal edges, external boundary connections, types, fan-out and runtime behavior remain correct after extraction; no unexpected dangling wires/ports.
- [ ] Cancel leaves the graph/library unchanged; success saves reusable definition and applies parent replacement consistently with current Save/Auto Save implementation.
- [ ] Reusable Subgraphs can still be inserted/edited from other graphs; restrictions on nested definitions, concrete sources/sinks and parent compatibility remain intact.
- [ ] Desktop and narrow layouts, pointer/keyboard/accessibility paths, and relevant automated tests pass.

## Implementation locations / verification

- [`extension/graph-editor.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js): heading click modifiers/selection, contextual action and count, `createSubgraph()`, dialog and `renderPortEditor()` disclosure.
- [`extension/subgraphs.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/subgraphs.js): preserve `extractSubgraph()`'s mapping contract; extend only where needed for safety or meaningful preview.
- [`extension/graph.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.css) and shared styles as necessary for selected-state affordances/dialog layout.
- [`tests/extension/subgraphs.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/subgraphs.spec.js), graph interaction and browser layout tests: cover modifier combinations, selecting/deselecting, focus, invalid selection, dialog default/advanced modes, failed validation, preservation of internal/external edges, fan-out, persisted/reused subgraphs and parent refresh/Undo.
- Update [`docs/extension-graph.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md) to describe the new discoverable workflow.

## Out of scope

- Drag-box/rubber-band selection (possible future improvement).
- Nested subgraphs / changing execution architecture.
- Removing advanced port editing entirely.
- Persistent undo/version history (owned by #299).

This issue is the UI/interaction simplification of the reusable-subgraph feature introduced by [#265](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/265).
